notes: ἐφ᾽ οἷς is written twice in English, as in and as the -of of whereof; the repetition rides inside the relative's unit as a helper under rule 103's function-word arm rather than added.
οἷς heads on things under rule 77's generic-noun arm; τότε heads on time, the noun the supplied frame is built on, and heading on that remains defensible.
ἐκείνων keeps of those things whole under rule 17's generic-noun clause, no article competing, and θάνατος carries the supplied copula under rule 63, its subject τέλος being a lexical noun.
